title: Before the show had a name
summary: Ben Taylor proposed a late-night programme of records, live acoustic music, and poetry, with Maxie Haddow-Allen producing. Local performers could come from the Catweazle Club and the Union Bar. The possible slots were 1–3am on a Monday or Wednesday.
music: An Aztec Camera song each week
A particularly long song each week
cues: Songs That Sound Better At The Wrong Speed
A French speaking clock giving the wrong time

title: The two-hour demo
summary: The post-demo notes say where Ben would tighten his links, where Maxie would adjust the levels, and where a pause should follow a performance. They also propose slipping from one version of ‘Dancing Queen’ into another at the right beat.
guests: Sam Willetts, poet, identified by Ben as a demo guest in April
evidence: The team wrote its assessment after making the demo.

title: Writing for the studio
summary: By January the opening had moved to four o’clock. Ben and Rufus had links between records. A poet and a musician each had time to come back for another piece. One jingle gives the show the mock announcement that it was filmed in front of a live studio audience.
cues: Batman-style jingles for the time check, tea break, and phone-in
Record scratches and a whispered ident
Several versions of the same song to end the show

title: The Sunday dry runs
summary: Three surviving demo sheets open with news, weather, an ident, and ‘Popcorn’. The early February version starts its records with Aztec Camera. Another opens with the Clash and leaves spaces for new releases.
evidence: 2 February is the save date of DEMO2.DOC. DEMO3.DOC was saved on 9 February. DEMO4.DOC is a later revision.

title: Eoin Quiery and the first Sunday
summary: The first running order puts ‘Teenage Kicks’ straight after the theme, then Television’s ‘Venus’ on vinyl. Eoin Quiery has three session slots. For Caroline Trettine’s ‘Be A Devil’, the operator is told to play thirty seconds at 45rpm, fade it, and start again at 33.
guests: Fraser – readings in the running order
music: Nick Drake – One of These Things First
cues: 16:03:20 – Shout over the start of Popcorn
17:22:39 – Jonathan Richman, I Was Dancing In The Lesbian Bar
evidence: A listener reported hearing the entire show on 20 February. Maxie later compared Eoin’s first-week session with Katie’s second-week one. These accounts establish both appearances; individual cues come from the running order.

title: Katie Buckhaven in session
summary: Katie Buckhaven’s three session entries are ‘Let Her Cry’, ‘It’s A Funny World’, and ‘Silver Dagger’. Between them sit White Town, Love, and Aztec Camera’s version of ‘Jump’. Klaus Wunderlich’s Hammond provides the music under the trivia slot.
evidence: Maxie wrote the following day about how Katie had sounded and the change in microphone levels since the first week.

title: George Kirby, Dave Dwan, and Professor Pea
summary: George Kirby is down for ‘To Ramona’, ‘I Cannot Yet Choose To Die’, and ‘I Feel Realer’. Dave Dwan has two readings and Professor Pea has a literary slot. The sheet marks two records that could be dropped if time ran short.
music: Lord Tanamo – I’m In The Mood for Ska
Trash Can Sinatras – To Sir With Love

title: Unclassified and Andreas Beltzer
summary: Unclassified were Julian Dickinson and Julia Middleton, on guitar, voice, and soprano sax. Their session shares the sheet with Catweazle host Andreas Beltzer’s readings. The detailed version makes room for Uncle Anton’s Problem Corner and Rufus testing the microphones.
guests: Unclassified – Julian Dickinson and Julia Middleton
evidence: In April Ben recorded that the duo had played and that Andreas had been on Dead Air the preceding term. The running order supplies the date and planned sequence.

title: An extra half-hour
summary: With News Review off the schedule, the station offered Ben an extra half-hour. The revised sheet runs to 17:58. It calls for three sessions from Superfly, readings by Sam, a fishing phone-in, and Echo and the Bunnymen’s ‘The Killing Moon’ before the theme.
music: Paul Simon – Late In The Evening
Bix Beiderbecke with Frankie Trumbauer and Eddie Lang – Singin’ the Blues
Echo and the Bunnymen – The Killing Moon
evidence: In April Ben confirmed that Sam had done the demo and one show in the previous term. The 16 March sheet lists him as Sam.

title: The April programmes
summary: April sheets arrange records by the Undertones, Jan & Dean, and Jonathan Richman alongside Eoin’s ‘The Time, The Place’ and ‘My First Cigarette’. A second list marks up Microdisney, Jimmy Cliff, and Everything but the Girl, with ‘Machine Gun’ by the Commodores as a music bed. On 26 April Ben wrote that an Ian Green session was due that week and three further songs were on MiniDisc.
guests: Ian Green – recorded guitar and vocal session
music: Jimmy Cliff – Many Rivers to Cross
evidence: The four April files are working lists and reading material. Only the email identifies the Ian Green recording and its intended week.

title: Dylan, without mentioning Dylan
summary: The joke in Ben’s pitch was to spend the whole show on Dylan covers and originals without mentioning what they had in common. The dated song sheet gives Eoin Quiery ‘Tangled Up In Blue’ and ‘Simple Twist of Fate’, and George Kirby a ten-minute ‘Sad Eyed Lady of the Lowlands’. The companion script gives Dylan Bedford a poetry slot.
guests: Dylan Bedford – poetry in the script
music: Aztec Camera – I Threw It All Away
Emmylou Harris – Every Grain of Sand
evidence: The source is headed ‘Dead Air 8/6/97 – Songs’. The newspaper listing quoted that morning announced Ben and Rufus with music and poetry.

title: The farewell that was a week early
summary: Ben proposed a farewell show whose running joke was that the programme still had another week to go. The June 15 list brings back Jonathan Richman, adds Robert Wyatt’s ‘Shipbuilding’, and revisits the phone box outside the station. The date comes from the saved file and the sequence in Ben’s May pitch.
music: Jonathan Richman – I Was Dancing In The Lesbian Bar
The Smiths – I Know It’s Over
Gram Parsons – Cry One More Time
cues: The Phone Box Outside the Station

title: Christmas in June
summary: The final June plan called for a Christmas special. Ben proposed a William Shatner-style spoken ‘Eternal Flame’ and a Rufus Doors orchestral ‘Every Loser Wins’ for the two sides of a Christmas single. On the morning of 22 June, the station confirmed Dan Lester would operate the desk from 3 to 5pm.
guests: Dan Lester – booked to operate the desk
evidence: The schedule and desk booking survive. The pitch records the Christmas items; it does not establish a recording or release of the single.
